title.zh: 卷七十一 志第二十四 律曆四
title.raw: 卷七十一 志第二十四 律曆四 Volume 71 Treatises 24: Measures and Calendar 4

sentences.zh: 道體為一，天地之元，萬物之祖也。

translations.literal: The substance of the Way is one—it is the origin of Heaven and Earth and the ancestor of all things.
translations.idiomatic: The Way is unified in essence; it is the root of Heaven and Earth and the source of all things.

sentences.zh: 散而為氣，則有陰有陽；

translations.literal: When it disperses and becomes qi, there is yin and there is yang;
translations.idiomatic: Diffused as breath, it yields yin and yang;

sentences.zh: 動而為數，則有奇有偶；

translations.literal: When it moves and becomes number, there is odd and there is even;
translations.idiomatic: set in motion as number, it yields odd and even;

sentences.zh: 凝而為形，則有剛有柔；

translations.literal: When it congeals and becomes form, there is hard and there is soft;
translations.idiomatic: condensed into form, it yields hard and soft;

sentences.zh: 發而為聲，則有清有濁，其著見而為器，則有律、有呂。

translations.literal: When it manifests as sound, there is clear and there is turbid; when it appears visibly as vessels, there are pitch pipes and secondary pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Expressed as sound, it yields clear and muddy tones; made manifest in instruments, it becomes the pitch pipes and the secondary pipes.

sentences.zh: 凡禮樂、刑法、權衡、度量皆出於是。

translations.literal: All ritual and music, penal law, weights and measures, and standards of length and capacity derive from this.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual, music, penal codes, weights, and measures all stem from this principle.

sentences.zh: 自周衰樂壞，而律呂候氣之法不傳。

translations.literal: From the decline of Zhou and the ruin of music, the method of pitch pipes awaiting the qi did not transmit.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou's decline and the collapse of proper music, the method of using pitch pipes to observe the seasonal qi was lost.

sentences.zh: 西漢劉歆、揚雄之徒，僅存其說。

translations.literal: In Western Han, Liu Xin, Yang Xiong, and others preserved only the theory.
translations.idiomatic: In the Western Han, Liu Xin, Yang Xiong, and their circle kept only the theory alive.

sentences.zh: 京房作準以代律，分六十聲，始于南事，終於去滅。

translations.literal: Jing Fang made the pitch standard to replace pitch pipes, dividing into sixty sounds, beginning with Nanshi and ending with Qumie.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang devised a tuning standard to substitute for the pitch pipes, dividing sound into sixty degrees from Nanshi to Qumie.

sentences.zh: 然聲細而難分，世不能用。

translations.literal: Yet the sounds were fine and hard to distinguish, and the age could not employ them.
translations.idiomatic: But the gradations were too fine to distinguish, and the world could not use them.

sentences.zh: 曆晉及隋、唐，律法微隱。

translations.literal: Through Jin and Sui and Tang, pitch law grew faint and obscure.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin through Sui and Tang, the science of pitch grew increasingly obscure.

sentences.zh: 《宋史》止載律呂大數，不獲其詳。

translations.literal: The History of Song records only the great numbers of pitch pipes and secondary pipes, without obtaining the details.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Song records only the broad figures for pitch pipes and secondary pipes, not the full particulars.

sentences.zh: 今掇仁宗論律及諸儒言鐘律者記於篇，以補續舊學之闕。

translations.literal: Now the present compilation records Emperor Renzong's discussions of pitch and the various scholars' remarks on bell pitch in this chapter, to supplement and continue what is missing in the old learning.
translations.idiomatic: Here we gather Emperor Renzong's treatise on pitch together with scholars' writings on bell pitch, to fill the gaps in the ancient tradition.

sentences.zh: 仁宗著《景祐樂髓新經》，凡六篇，述七宗二變及管分陰陽、剖析清濁，歸之於本律。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong authored the New Classic of the Marrow of Music of the Jingyou era, six chapters in all, setting forth the seven foundations and two variants, dividing pipes into yin and yang, analyzing clear and turbid, and returning them to the fundamental pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong wrote the New Classic of the Marrow of Music of the Jingyou reign in six sections, explaining the seven root tones and two variant tones, assigning yin and yang to the pipes, distinguishing clear from turbid sounds, and tracing them all back to the fundamental pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 次及間聲，合古今之樂，參之以六壬遁甲。

translations.literal: Next it treats intermediate sounds, combining music ancient and modern, and cross-referencing with the six-ren and dunjia methods.
translations.idiomatic: It goes on to treat intermediate tones, reconciling ancient and modern music and correlating them with the six-ren and dunjia divination systems.

sentences.zh: 其一、釋十二均，曰：「黃鐘之宮為子、為神後、為土、為雞緩、為正宮調，太簇商為寅、為功曹、為金、為般頡、為大石調，姑洗角為辰、為天剛、為木、為嗢沒斯、為小石角，林鐘徵為未、為小吉、為火、為雲漢、為黃鐘徵，南呂羽為酉，為從魁、為水、為滴、為般涉調，應鐘變宮為亥、為登明、為日、為密、為中管黃鐘宮，蕤賓變徵為午、為勝先、為月、為莫、為應鐘徵。

translations.literal: First, it explains the twelve scales, saying: "The gong of Yellow Bell corresponds to zi, to Shendu, to earth, to Jihuan, and to the Zhenggong mode; the shang of Great Cluster corresponds to yin, to Gongcao, to metal, to Banjie, and to the Dashi mode; the jue of Maiden Washing corresponds to chen, to Tiangang, to wood, to Womosi, and to the Xiaoshi jue; the zhi of Forest Bell corresponds to wei, to Xiaoji, to fire, to Yunhan, and to the Yellow Bell zhi; the yu of Southern Pipe corresponds to you, to Congkui, to water, to Di, and to the Banshe mode; the bian gong of Responding Bell corresponds to hai, to Dengming, to the sun, to Mi, and to the mid-pipe Yellow Bell gong; the bian zhi of Embellished Guest corresponds to wu, to Shengxian, to the moon, to Mo, and to the Responding Bell zhi."
translations.idiomatic: The first section explains the twelve scales: "The Yellow Bell gong is zi, Shendu, earth, Jihuan, and the Zhenggong mode; the Great Cluster shang is yin, Gongcao, metal, Banjie, and the Dashi mode; the Maiden Washing jue is chen, Tiangang, wood, Womosi, and the Xiaoshi jue; the Forest Bell zhi is wei, Xiaoji, fire, Yunhan, and the Yellow Bell zhi; the Southern Pipe yu is you, Congkui, water, Di, and the Banshe mode; the Responding Bell bian gong is hai, Dengming, the sun, Mi, and the mid-pipe Yellow Bell gong; the Embellished Guest bian zhi is wu, Shengxian, the moon, Mo, and the Responding Bell zhi."

sentences.zh: 大呂之宮為大吉、為高宮，夾鐘商為大沖、為高大石，仲呂角為太一、為中管小石調，夷則徵為傳送、為大呂徵，無射羽為河魁、為高般涉，黃鐘變宮為正宮調，林鐘變徵為黃鐘徵。

translations.literal: The gong of Great Pitch corresponds to Daji and to the Gaogong mode; the shang of Pinched Bell corresponds to Dachong and to the Gaodashi mode; the jue of Second Pitch corresponds to Taiyi and to the mid-pipe Xiaoshi mode; the zhi of Ethereal Pitch corresponds to Chuansong and to the Great Pitch zhi; the yu of Wushe corresponds to Hekui and to the Gaobanshe mode; the bian gong of Yellow Bell is the Zhenggong mode; the bian zhi of Forest Bell is the Yellow Bell zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Pitch gong is Daji and the Gaogong mode; the Pinched Bell shang is Dachong and the Gaodashi mode; the Second Pitch jue is Taiyi and the mid-pipe Xiaoshi mode; the Ethereal Pitch zhi is Chuansong and the Great Pitch zhi; the Wushe yu is Hekui and the Gaobanshe mode; the Yellow Bell bian gong is the Zhenggong mode; the Forest Bell bian zhi is the Yellow Bell zhi.

sentences.zh: 太簇之宮為中管高宮，姑洗商為高大石，蕤賓角為歇指角，南呂徵為太簇徵，應鐘羽為中管高般涉，大呂變宮為高宮，夷則變徵為大呂徵。

translations.literal: The gong of Great Cluster is the mid-pipe Gaogong mode; the shang of Maiden Washing is the Gaodashi mode; the jue of Embellished Guest is the Xiezhi jue; the zhi of Southern Pipe is the Great Cluster zhi; the yu of Responding Bell is the mid-pipe Gaobanshe mode; the bian gong of Great Pitch is the Gaogong mode; the bian zhi of Ethereal Pitch is the Great Pitch zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Cluster gong is the mid-pipe Gaogong mode; the Maiden Washing shang is the Gaodashi mode; the Embellished Guest jue is the Xiezhi jue; the Southern Pipe zhi is the Great Cluster zhi; the Responding Bell yu is the mid-pipe Gaobanshe mode; the Great Pitch bian gong is the Gaogong mode; the Ethereal Pitch bian zhi is the Great Pitch zhi.

sentences.zh: 夾鐘之宮為中呂宮，仲呂商為雙調，林鐘角在今樂亦為林鐘角，無射徵為夾鐘徵，黃鐘羽為中呂調，太簇變宮為中管高宮，南呂變徵為太簇徵。

translations.literal: The gong of Pinched Bell is the Zhonglü gong mode; the shang of Second Pitch is the Shuangdiao mode; the jue of Forest Bell in present music is also the Forest Bell jue; the zhi of Wushe is the Pinched Bell zhi; the yu of Yellow Bell is the Zhonglü mode; the bian gong of Great Cluster is the mid-pipe Gaogong mode; the bian zhi of Southern Pipe is the Great Cluster zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Pinched Bell gong is the Zhonglü gong mode; the Second Pitch shang is the Shuangdiao mode; the Forest Bell jue in current music is likewise the Forest Bell jue; the Wushe zhi is the Pinched Bell zhi; the Yellow Bell yu is the Zhonglü mode; the Great Cluster bian gong is the mid-pipe Gaogong mode; the Southern Pipe bian zhi is the Great Cluster zhi.

sentences.zh: 姑洗之宮為中管中呂宮，蕤賓商為中管商調，夷則角為中管林鐘角，應鐘徵為姑洗徵，大呂羽為中管中呂調，夾鐘變宮為中呂宮，無射變徵為夾鐘徵。

translations.literal: The gong of Maiden Washing is the mid-pipe Zhonglü gong mode; the shang of Embellished Guest is the mid-pipe shang mode; the jue of Ethereal Pitch is the mid-pipe Forest Bell jue; the zhi of Responding Bell is the Maiden Washing zhi; the yu of Great Pitch is the mid-pipe Zhonglü mode; the bian gong of Pinched Bell is the Zhonglü gong mode; the bian zhi of Wushe is the Pinched Bell zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Maiden Washing gong is the mid-pipe Zhonglü gong mode; the Embellished Guest shang is the mid-pipe shang mode; the Ethereal Pitch jue is the mid-pipe Forest Bell jue; the Responding Bell zhi is the Maiden Washing zhi; the Great Pitch yu is the mid-pipe Zhonglü mode; the Pinched Bell bian gong is the Zhonglü gong mode; the Wushe bian zhi is the Pinched Bell zhi.

sentences.zh: 仲呂之宮為道調宮，林鐘商為小石調，南呂角為越調，黃鐘徵為中呂徵，太簇羽為平調，姑洗變宮為中管中呂宮，應鐘變徵為姑洗徵。

translations.literal: The gong of Second Pitch is the Daodiao gong mode; the shang of Forest Bell is the Xiaoshi mode; the jue of Southern Pipe is the Yuediao mode; the zhi of Yellow Bell is the Zhonglü zhi; the yu of Great Cluster is the Pingdiao mode; the bian gong of Maiden Washing is the mid-pipe Zhonglü gong mode; the bian zhi of Responding Bell is the Maiden Washing zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Second Pitch gong is the Daodiao gong mode; the Forest Bell shang is the Xiaoshi mode; the Southern Pipe jue is the Yuediao mode; the Yellow Bell zhi is the Zhonglü zhi; the Great Cluster yu is the Pingdiao mode; the Maiden Washing bian gong is the mid-pipe Zhonglü gong mode; the Responding Bell bian zhi is the Maiden Washing zhi.

sentences.zh: 蕤賓之宮為中管道調宮，夷則商為中管小石調，無射角為中管越調，大呂徵為蕤賓徵，夾鐘羽為中管平調，中呂變宮為道調宮，黃鐘變徵為仲呂徵，林鐘之宮為南呂宮，南呂商為歇指調，應鐘角為大石調，太簇微為林鐘徵，姑洗羽為高平調，蕤賓變宮為中管道調宮，大呂變徵為蕤賓徵。

translations.literal: The gong of Embellished Guest is the mid-pipe Daodiao gong mode; the shang of Ethereal Pitch is the mid-pipe Xiaoshi mode; the jue of Wushe is the mid-pipe Yuediao mode; the zhi of Great Pitch is the Embellished Guest zhi; the yu of Pinched Bell is the mid-pipe Pingdiao mode; the bian gong of Second Pitch is the Daodiao gong mode; the bian zhi of Yellow Bell is the Second Pitch zhi. The gong of Forest Bell is the Southern Pipe gong mode; the shang of Southern Pipe is the Xiezhi mode; the jue of Responding Bell is the Dashi mode; the zhi of Great Cluster is the Forest Bell zhi; the yu of Maiden Washing is the Gaoping mode; the bian gong of Embellished Guest is the mid-pipe Daodiao gong mode; the bian zhi of Great Pitch is the Embellished Guest zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Embellished Guest gong is the mid-pipe Daodiao gong mode; the Ethereal Pitch shang is the mid-pipe Xiaoshi mode; the Wushe jue is the mid-pipe Yuediao mode; the Great Pitch zhi is the Embellished Guest zhi; the Pinched Bell yu is the mid-pipe Pingdiao mode; the Second Pitch bian gong is the Daodiao gong mode; the Yellow Bell bian zhi is the Second Pitch zhi. The Forest Bell gong is the Southern Pipe gong mode; the Southern Pipe shang is the Xiezhi mode; the Responding Bell jue is the Dashi mode; the Great Cluster zhi is the Forest Bell zhi; the Maiden Washing yu is the Gaoping mode; the Embellished Guest bian gong is the mid-pipe Daodiao gong mode; the Great Pitch bian zhi is the Embellished Guest zhi.

sentences.zh: 夷則之宮為仙呂，無射商為林鐘商，黃鐘角為高大石調，夾鐘徵為夷則徵，仲呂羽為仙呂調，林鐘變宮為南呂宮，太簇變徵為林鐘徵。

translations.literal: The gong of Ethereal Pitch is Xianlü; the shang of Wushe is the Forest Bell shang; the jue of Yellow Bell is the Gaodashi mode; the zhi of Pinched Bell is the Ethereal Pitch zhi; the yu of Second Pitch is the Xianlü mode; the bian gong of Forest Bell is the Southern Pipe gong mode; the bian zhi of Great Cluster is the Forest Bell zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Ethereal Pitch gong is Xianlü; the Wushe shang is the Forest Bell shang; the Yellow Bell jue is the Gaodashi mode; the Pinched Bell zhi is the Ethereal Pitch zhi; the Second Pitch yu is the Xianlü mode; the Forest Bell bian gong is the Southern Pipe gong mode; the Great Cluster bian zhi is the Forest Bell zhi.

sentences.zh: 南呂之宮為中管仙呂宮，應鐘商為中管林鐘商，大呂角為中管高大石角，姑洗徵為南呂徵，蕤賓羽為中管仙呂調，夷則變宮為仙呂宮，夾鐘變徵為夷則徵。

translations.literal: The gong of Southern Pipe is the mid-pipe Xianlü gong mode; the shang of Responding Bell is the mid-pipe Forest Bell shang; the jue of Great Pitch is the mid-pipe Gaodashi jue; the zhi of Maiden Washing is the Southern Pipe zhi; the yu of Embellished Guest is the mid-pipe Xianlü mode; the bian gong of Ethereal Pitch is the Xianlü gong mode; the bian zhi of Pinched Bell is the Ethereal Pitch zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Pipe gong is the mid-pipe Xianlü gong mode; the Responding Bell shang is the mid-pipe Forest Bell shang; the Great Pitch jue is the mid-pipe Gaodashi jue; the Maiden Washing zhi is the Southern Pipe zhi; the Embellished Guest yu is the mid-pipe Xianlü mode; the Ethereal Pitch bian gong is the Xianlü gong mode; the Pinched Bell bian zhi is the Ethereal Pitch zhi.

sentences.zh: 無射之宮為黃鐘宮，黃鐘商為越調，太簇角為變角，仲呂徵為無射徵，林鐘羽為黃鐘羽，南呂變宮為中管仙呂宮，姑洗變徵為南呂徵。

translations.literal: The gong of Wushe is the Yellow Bell gong mode; the shang of Yellow Bell is the Yuediao mode; the jue of Great Cluster is the bian jue; the zhi of Second Pitch is the Wushe zhi; the yu of Forest Bell is the Yellow Bell yu; the bian gong of Southern Pipe is the mid-pipe Xianlü gong mode; the bian zhi of Maiden Washing is the Southern Pipe zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Wushe gong is the Yellow Bell gong mode; the Yellow Bell shang is the Yuediao mode; the Great Cluster jue is the bian jue; the Second Pitch zhi is the Wushe zhi; the Forest Bell yu is the Yellow Bell yu; the Southern Pipe bian gong is the mid-pipe Xianlü gong mode; the Maiden Washing bian zhi is the Southern Pipe zhi.

sentences.zh: 應鐘之宮為中管黃鐘宮，大呂商為中管越調，夾鐘角為中管雙角，蕤賓徵為應鐘徵，夷則羽為中管黃鐘羽，無射變宮為黃鐘宮，仲呂變徵為無射徵。」

translations.literal: The gong of Responding Bell is the mid-pipe Yellow Bell gong mode; the shang of Great Pitch is the mid-pipe Yuediao mode; the jue of Pinched Bell is the mid-pipe shuang jue; the zhi of Embellished Guest is the Responding Bell zhi; the yu of Ethereal Pitch is the mid-pipe Yellow Bell yu; the bian gong of Wushe is the Yellow Bell gong mode; the bian zhi of Second Pitch is the Wushe zhi."
translations.idiomatic: The Responding Bell gong is the mid-pipe Yellow Bell gong mode; the Great Pitch shang is the mid-pipe Yuediao mode; the Pinched Bell jue is the mid-pipe shuang jue; the Embellished Guest zhi is the Responding Bell zhi; the Ethereal Pitch yu is the mid-pipe Yellow Bell yu; the Wushe bian gong is the Yellow Bell gong mode; the Second Pitch bian zhi is the Wushe zhi."

sentences.zh: 二、明所主事，調五聲為五行、五事、四時、五帝、五神、五嶽、五味、五色，為生數一二三四五、成數六七八九十，為五藏、五官及五星。

translations.literal: Second, it clarifies what each governs, aligning the five tones with the five phases, five affairs, four seasons, five emperors, five spirits, five sacred peaks, five flavors, and five colors, with the generating numbers one through five and the completing numbers six through ten, and with the five viscera, five sense organs, and five stars.
translations.idiomatic: Second, it explains what each tone governs, correlating the five tones with the five phases, five affairs, four seasons, five emperors, five spirits, five sacred peaks, five flavors, and five colors, with the generating numbers one through five and completing numbers six through ten, and with the five viscera, five sense organs, and five planets.

sentences.zh: 三、辯音聲，曰：「宮聲沈厚粗大而下，為君，聲調則國安，亂則荒而危。

translations.literal: Third, it distinguishes sounds, saying: "The gong tone is deep, thick, large, coarse, and descending; it is the ruler. When the tone is correct, the state is secure; when disordered, there is desolation and peril."
translations.idiomatic: Third, it distinguishes the tones: "The gong tone is deep, full, broad, and heavy, descending in pitch; it represents the ruler. When it is in tune, the state is secure; when it falls into disorder, the realm grows desolate and endangered."

sentences.zh: 合口通音謂之宮，其聲雄洪，屬平聲，西域言'婆陀力'。

translations.literal: Closing the mouth to produce a continuous sound is called gong; its sound is bold and resounding, belonging to the level tone; in the Western Regions it is called 'Potuoli.'
translations.idiomatic: A closed-mouth, sustained tone is called gong; its sound is bold and resonant, of the level tone; in the Western Regions it is called 'Potuoli.'

sentences.zh: 一曰婆陀力。

translations.literal: It is also called Potuoli.
translations.idiomatic: That is, Potuoli.

sentences.zh: 商聲勁凝明達，上而下歸於中，為臣，聲調則刑法不作，威令行，亂則其宮壞。

translations.literal: The shang tone is forceful, firm, bright, and penetrating, descending from above and returning to the center; it is the minister. When the tone is correct, penal law is not misapplied and authority is enforced; when disordered, the gong is ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The shang tone is forceful, firm, bright, and clear, falling from above toward the center; it represents the minister. When it is in tune, penal law is not abused and commands are obeyed; when it falls into disorder, the gong tone is ruined.

sentences.zh: 開口吐聲謂之商，音將將、倉倉然，西域言'稽識'。

translations.literal: Opening the mouth to emit sound is called shang; its sound is jiangjiang and cangcang; in the Western Regions it is called 'Jishi.'
translations.idiomatic: An open-mouth, exhaled tone is called shang; its sound is ringing and resonant; in the Western Regions it is called 'Jishi.'

sentences.zh: '稽識'，猶長聲也。

translations.literal: 'Jishi' is like a prolonged tone.
translations.idiomatic: 'Jishi' means a drawn-out tone.

sentences.zh: 角聲長而通徹，中平而正，為民，聲調則四民安，亂則人怨。

translations.literal: The jue tone is long and penetrating, level at the center and upright; it is the people. When the tone is correct, the four classes of people are secure; when disordered, the people resent.
translations.idiomatic: The jue tone is long and penetrating, centered and even; it represents the people. When it is in tune, the four classes of society are at peace; when it falls into disorder, the people grow resentful.

sentences.zh: 聲出齒間謂之角，喔喔、確確然，西域言'沙識'，猶質直聲也。

translations.literal: Sound issuing from between the teeth is called jue; it is woowo and queque; in the Western Regions it is called 'Shashi,' like a plain, direct sound.
translations.idiomatic: A tone produced between the teeth is called jue; its sound is woowo and queque; in the Western Regions it is called 'Shashi,' a plain, straightforward tone.

sentences.zh: 徵聲抑揚流利，從下而上歸於中，為事，聲調則百事理，亂則事隳。

translations.literal: The zhi tone rises and falls smoothly, ascending from below and returning to the center; it is affairs. When the tone is correct, the hundred affairs are ordered; when disordered, affairs collapse.
translations.idiomatic: The zhi tone rises and falls in flowing cadence, ascending from below toward the center; it represents affairs. When it is in tune, the hundred affairs are well ordered; when it falls into disorder, affairs collapse.

sentences.zh: 齒合而唇啟謂之徵，倚倚、栎戲栎戲然，西域言'沙臘'。

translations.literal: Teeth closed and lips parted is called zhi; it is yiyi and lixi lixi; in the Western Regions it is called 'Shala.'
translations.idiomatic: With teeth closed and lips parted is called zhi; its sound is yiyi and lixi lixi; in the Western Regions it is called 'Shala.'

sentences.zh: '沙臘'，和也。

translations.literal: 'Shala' means harmony.
translations.idiomatic: 'Shala' means harmonious.

sentences.zh: 羽聲喓喓而遠徹，細小而高，為物，聲調則倉稟實、庶物備，亂則匱竭。

translations.literal: The yu tone is yaoya and far-reaching, fine and high; it is things. When the tone is correct, granaries are full and the myriad things are provided; when disordered, there is exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: The yu tone is yaoya and far-carrying, fine and high in pitch; it represents things. When it is in tune, the granaries are full and all things are supplied; when it falls into disorder, stores run empty.

sentences.zh: 齒開唇聚謂之羽，詡、雨、酗、芋然。

translations.literal: Teeth open and lips gathered is called yu; it is like xu, yu, xu, and yu.
translations.idiomatic: With teeth open and lips gathered is called yu; its sound resembles xu, yu, xu, and yu.

sentences.zh: 西域言'般瞻'。

translations.literal: In the Western Regions it is called 'Banzhan.'
translations.idiomatic: Within the Western Regions it is called 'Banzhan.'

sentences.zh: 變宮，西域言'侯利箑'，猶言'斛律'聲也。

translations.literal: The bian gong—in the Western Regions it is called 'Houliqie,' like the sound 'Hulü.'
translations.idiomatic: The bian gong—in the Western Regions it is called 'Houliqie,' akin to the sound 'Hulü.'

sentences.zh: 變徵聲，西域言'沙侯加濫'，猶應聲也。」

translations.literal: The bian zhi tone—in the Western Regions it is called 'Shahoujialan,' like a responding sound."
translations.idiomatic: The bian zhi tone—in the Western Regions it is called 'Shahoujialan,' like a responsive tone."

sentences.zh: 其四、明律呂相生，祭天地宗廟，配律陽之數，曰：「太空，育五太：太易、太初、太始、太素、太極也。

translations.literal: Fourth, it clarifies the mutual generation of pitch pipes and secondary pipes, sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples, and matches the yang numbers of the pitch pipes, saying: "The Great Void nurtures the five Greats: Great Change, Great Beginning, Great Start, Great Simplicity, and the Supreme Ultimate."
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, it explains how pitch pipes and secondary pipes generate one another, the rites of sacrifice to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples, and the yang numbers assigned to the pitch pipes: "The Great Void gives rise to the five Greats—Great Change, Great Beginning, Great Start, Great Simplicity, and the Supreme Ultimate."

sentences.zh: 分為七政，陽數七，所以齊律呂、均節度，不可加減也。

translations.literal: It divides into the seven regulators; the yang number is seven, by which pitch pipes and secondary pipes are aligned and measures are equalized—nothing may be added or subtracted.
translations.idiomatic: It divides into the seven regulators; seven is the yang number by which pitch pipes and secondary pipes are harmonized and measures standardized—nothing may be added or subtracted.

sentences.zh: 以育六甲，六甲，天之使，行風雹，筴鬼神。

translations.literal: From this the six jia are nurtured; the six jia are Heaven's envoys, bringing wind and hail, and divining spirits and ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: From this the six jia are produced; the six jia are Heaven's emissaries, driving wind and hail and divining the spirits.

sentences.zh: 為歲日時有善惡，故為九宮。

translations.literal: Because years, days, and hours have good and evil, there are the nine palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Because years, days, and hours hold good and ill fortune, there are the nine palaces.

sentences.zh: 九者，陽數變化之道也。

translations.literal: Nine is the way of change in yang numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Nine is the path of transformation within yang numbers.

sentences.zh: 為四正卦、五行、十幹，陰陽錯綜，律呂相葉，命宮而商者應，修下而高者降，下生隔八，上生隔六，皆圖于左。」

translations.literal: It becomes the four cardinal hexagrams, the five phases, and the ten stems; yin and yang interweave, pitch pipes and secondary pipes correspond, the gong is appointed and the shang responds, what is long below and high above descends, downward generation skips eight, upward generation skips six—all are diagrammed at left."
translations.idiomatic: It yields the four cardinal hexagrams, the five phases, and the ten heavenly stems; yin and yang intertwine, pitch pipes and secondary pipes answer one another, the gong is set and the shang responds, the long below and high above descend, downward generation skips eight steps and upward generation skips six—all are charted on the left."

sentences.zh: 其五、著十二管短長。

translations.literal: Fifth, it sets forth the lengths of the twelve pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, it records the lengths of the twelve pipes.

sentences.zh: 其六、出度量衡，辯古今尺龠。

translations.literal: Sixth, it presents measures, weights, and balances, and distinguishes ancient and modern foot-rules and pitch tubes.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, it presents measures, weights, and balances, and distinguishes ancient and modern foot-rules and pitch tubes.

sentences.zh: 律呂真聲，本陰陽之氣，可以感格天地，在於符合尺寸短長，宜因聲以定之。

translations.literal: The true sounds of pitch pipes and secondary pipes originate in the qi of yin and yang and can move and harmonize Heaven and Earth; the key lies in matching the dimensions of length and shortness, and they should be fixed by sound.
translations.idiomatic: The true tones of pitch pipes and secondary pipes arise from yin and yang qi and can move Heaven and Earth; the essential point is that their dimensions match their lengths, and they should be determined from sound.

sentences.zh: 因聲定律，則庶幾為得；

translations.literal: Fixing pitch by sound, one may nearly attain correctness;
translations.idiomatic: When pitch is set from sound, one may nearly get it right;

sentences.zh: 以尺定聲，則乖隔甚矣。

translations.literal: fixing sound by the foot-rule, the discrepancy is very great.
translations.idiomatic: but when sound is fixed by the foot-rule, the error is very great.

sentences.zh: 初，馮元等上《新修景祐廣樂記》時，鄭保信、阮逸、胡瑗等奏造鐘律，詔翰林學士丁度、知制誥胥偃、右司諫高若訥、韓琦，取保信、逸、瑗等鐘律詳考得失。

translations.literal: Initially, when Feng Yuan and others presented the Newly Revised Comprehensive Record of Music of the Jingyou Era, Zheng Baoxin, Ruan Yi, Hu Yuan, and others memorialized to cast bells and pitch pipes. An edict ordered Hanlin Academician Ding Du, Drafting Edict Officer Xu Yan, Right Remonstrance Officer Gao Ruone, and Han Qi to take the bells and pitch pipes of Baoxin, Yi, Yuan, and others and examine them in detail for strengths and flaws.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Yuan and others first submitted the Newly Revised Comprehensive Record of Music of the Jingyou reign, Zheng Baoxin, Ruan Yi, Hu Yuan, and others memorialized to cast bells and pitch pipes. The throne ordered Hanlin Academician Ding Du, Drafting Edict Officer Xu Yan, Right Remonstrance Officer Gao Ruone, and Han Qi to examine the bells and pitch pipes made by Baoxin, Yi, Yuan, and others in detail for their merits and defects.

sentences.zh: 度等上議曰：「保信所制尺，用上黨秬黍圓者一黍之長，累而成尺。

translations.literal: Du and others submitted a memorial saying: "The foot-rule made by Baoxin used the length of one round black millet grain from Shangdang, accumulated to form a foot.
translations.idiomatic: Du and the others submitted a memorial stating: "The foot-rule made by Baoxin used the length of one round black millet grain from Shangdang, stacked to form a foot.

sentences.zh: 律管一，據尺裁九十黍之長，空徑三分，空圍九分，容秬黍千二百。

translations.literal: One pitch pipe, cut according to the foot-rule to the length of ninety millet grains, with an inner diameter of three fen and inner circumference of nine fen, holding twelve hundred black millet grains.
translations.idiomatic: One pitch pipe, cut to the length of ninety millet grains by the foot-rule, with an inner diameter of three fen and inner circumference of nine fen, holding twelve hundred black millet grains.

sentences.zh: 遂用黍長為分，再累成尺，校保信尺、律不同。

translations.literal: Then using the length of millet as fen and accumulating again to form a foot, when compared with Baoxin's foot-rule and pitch pipe, they differed.
translations.idiomatic: Then, using the length of millet as fen and stacking again to form a foot, this differed from Baoxin's foot-rule and pitch pipe.

sentences.zh: 其龠、合、升、鬥深闊，推以演算法，類皆差舛，不合周、漢量法。

translations.literal: The depth and width of the yue, he, sheng, and dou vessels, deduced by computational methods, were all in error and did not accord with the measures of Zhou and Han.
translations.idiomatic: The depth and width of the yue, he, sheng, and dou vessels, calculated by computational methods, were all in error and did not accord with Zhou and Han measures.

sentences.zh: 逸、瑗所制，亦上黨秬黍中者累廣求尺，制黃鐘之律。

translations.literal: What Yi and Yuan made also used medium black millet grains from Shangdang, accumulated in width to obtain a foot, and made the Yellow Bell pitch pipe.
translations.idiomatic: What Yi and Yuan made also used medium black millet grains from Shangdang, stacked in width to obtain a foot, and fashioned the Yellow Bell pitch pipe.

sentences.zh: 今用再累成尺，比逸、瑗所制，又復不同。

translations.literal: Now using accumulation again to form a foot and comparing with what Yi and Yuan made, they again differ.
translations.idiomatic: Now, using stacked grains again to form a foot and comparing with what Yi and Yuan made, they again differ.

sentences.zh: 至於律管、龠、合升、鬥、斛、豆、區、鬴亦率類是。

translations.literal: As for pitch pipes, yue, he, sheng, dou, hu, dou, qu, and fu vessels, they are generally of the same kind.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch pipes, yue, he, sheng, dou, hu, dou, qu, and fu vessels were generally the same in this respect.

sentences.zh: 蓋黍有圓長、大小而保信所用者圓黍，又首尾相銜，逸等止用大者，故再考之即不同。

translations.literal: For millet has round and long forms and large and small sizes; Baoxin used round millet, with head and tail linked end to end, while Yi and others used only the large grains—thus when examined again they differ.
translations.idiomatic: Millet comes in round and long forms and in large and small sizes; Baoxin used round millet with head and tail linked end to end, while Yi and the others used only the large grains—so when reexamined they differed.

sentences.zh: 尺既有差，故難以定鐘、磬。

translations.literal: Since the foot-rule already had discrepancies, bells and chime-stones were hard to fix.
translations.idiomatic: Because the foot-rule already differed, bells and chime-stones could not be reliably fixed.

sentences.zh: 謹詳古今之制，自晉至隋，累黍之法，但求尺裁管，不以權量參校，故歷代黃鐘之管容黍之數不同。

translations.literal: We have carefully examined the systems ancient and modern: from Jin through Sui, the method of accumulating millet sought only to cut pipes by the foot-rule and did not cross-check with weights and measures; thus the number of millet grains held by the Yellow Bell pipe differed through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: We have carefully examined ancient and modern systems: from Jin through Sui, the method of accumulating millet sought only to cut pipes by the foot-rule and did not cross-check with weights and measures; thus the number of millet grains held by the Yellow Bell pipe differed from dynasty to dynasty.

sentences.zh: 惟後周掘地得古玉鬥，據鬥造律，兼制權量，亦不同周、漢制度。

translations.literal: Only in Later Zhou, when an ancient jade dou was excavated from the ground, pitch pipes were made according to the dou and weights and measures were also fashioned—but these too differed from the Zhou and Han systems.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Later Zhou, when an ancient jade dou was excavated, pitch pipes were made according to the dou and weights and measures were also fashioned—but these too differed from the Zhou and Han systems.

sentences.zh: 故《漢志》有備數、和聲、審度、嘉量、權衡之說，悉起于黃鐘。

translations.literal: Thus the Han Treatise has the doctrines of complete numbers, harmonious sound, careful measurement, excellent capacity, and weights and balances—all originating from Yellow Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Han Treatise speaks of complete numbers, harmonious sound, careful measurement, excellent capacity, and weights and balances—all originating from Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 今欲數器之制參互無失，則《班志》積分之法為近。

translations.literal: If one now wishes the systems of numbers and vessels to cross-check without error, the method of accumulated parts in the Ban Treatise is nearest.
translations.idiomatic: If one now wishes the systems of numbers and vessels to cross-check without error, the method of accumulated parts in the Ban Treatise is the closest approach.

sentences.zh: 逸等以大黍累尺、小黍實龠，自戾本法。

translations.literal: Yi and others used large millet to accumulate the foot and small millet to fill the yue, departing from the original method on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and others used large millet to stack the foot and small millet to fill the yue, departing from the original method on their own.

sentences.zh: 保信黍尺以長為分，雖合後魏公孫崇所說，然當時已不施用，況保信今尺以圓黍累之，及首尾相銜，有與實龠之黍再累成尺不同。

translations.literal: Baoxin's millet foot-rule used length as fen; although this accorded with what Gongsun Chong of Later Wei said, it was already not employed at the time—how much more so now, when Baoxin's foot-rule accumulates round millet with head and tail linked end to end, which differs from using the millet that fills the yue to accumulate again into a foot.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxin's millet foot-rule used length as fen; although this matched what Gongsun Chong of Later Wei said, it was already obsolete even then—how much more so now, when Baoxin's foot-rule stacks round millet with head and tail linked end to end, which differs from using the millet that fills the yue to stack again into a foot.

sentences.zh: 其量器，分寸既不合古，即權衡之法不可獨用。

translations.literal: As for the capacity vessels, since the fen and cun already did not accord with antiquity, the method of weights and balances cannot be used alone.
translations.idiomatic: As for the capacity vessels, since the fen and cun already did not accord with antiquity, the method of weights and balances cannot be used by itself.

sentences.zh: 」詔悉罷之。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered all of them abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered all of them abolished.

sentences.zh: 又詔度等詳定太府寺並保信、逸、瑗所制尺，度等言：

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Du and others to examine in detail the foot-rules of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and those made by Baoxin, Yi, and Yuan. Du and others said:
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered Du and others to examine in detail the foot-rules of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and those made by Baoxin, Yi, and Yuan. Du and the others stated:

sentences.zh: 尺度之興尚矣，《周官》璧羨以起度，廣徑八寸，袤一尺。

translations.literal: The rise of foot-rules and measures is of long standing; the Rites of Zhou uses the bi-yan to establish measure, eight cun in width and diameter, one chi in length.
translations.idiomatic: The origin of foot-rules and measures goes far back; the Rites of Zhou uses the bi-yan to establish measure, eight cun in width and diameter and one chi in length.

sentences.zh: 《禮記》布手為尺，《淮南子》十二粟為一寸，《孫子》十厘為分，十分為寸，雖存異說，其可適從。

translations.literal: The Book of Rites takes the span of the hand as a foot; the Huainanzi says twelve grains make one cun; the Sunzi says ten li make one fen and ten fen make one cun—although differing accounts survive, which may be followed?
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites takes the span of the hand as a foot; the Huainanzi says twelve grains make one cun; the Sunzi says ten li make one fen and ten fen make one cun—although differing accounts survive, which should be followed?

sentences.zh: 《漢志》，元始中，召天下通知鐘律者百餘人，使劉歆典領之。

translations.literal: The Han Treatise records that in the Yuanshi era, more than a hundred persons throughout the realm versed in bells and pitch were summoned, and Liu Xin was put in charge.
translations.idiomatic: This Han Treatise records that in the Yuanshi era, more than a hundred persons throughout the realm versed in bells and pitch were summoned, and Liu Xin was put in charge.

sentences.zh: 是時，周滅二百餘年，古之律度當有考者。

translations.literal: At that time, more than two hundred years had passed since Zhou's fall; the pitch pipes and measures of antiquity ought to have been investigable.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, more than two hundred years had passed since the fall of Zhou; the pitch pipes and measures of antiquity ought still to have been investigable.

sentences.zh: 以歆之博貫藝文，曉達曆算，有所製作，宜不凡近。

translations.literal: Given Xin's broad mastery of arts and letters and clear understanding of calendrics and computation, whatever he produced ought not to have been ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Given Xin's broad mastery of arts and letters and his clear understanding of calendrics and computation, whatever he produced ought not to have been ordinary.

sentences.zh: 其審度之法云：「一黍之廣為分，十分為寸，十寸為尺。

translations.literal: His method of careful measurement says: "The width of one millet grain is one fen; ten fen make one cun; ten cun make one chi."
translations.idiomatic: His method of careful measurement states: "The width of one millet grain is one fen; ten fen make one cun; ten cun make one chi."

sentences.zh: 」先儒訓解經籍多引以為義，曆世祖襲，著之定法。

translations.literal: " Earlier scholars in annotating the classics often cited this as authoritative, and successive emperors inherited it and established it as fixed law.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier scholars, in annotating the classics, often cited this as authoritative, and successive emperors inherited it and established it as fixed law.

sentences.zh: 然而歲有豐儉，地有磽肥，就令一歲之中，一境之內，取以校驗，亦復不齊。

translations.literal: Yet years have abundance and scarcity, and lands have barrenness and fertility; even within one year and within one region, taking grains to verify, they are still not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Yet years vary between abundance and scarcity, and lands vary between barren and fertile; even within a single year and a single region, grains taken for verification still do not match.

sentences.zh: 是蓋天物之生，理難均一，古之立法，存其大概爾。

translations.literal: This is because things born of Heaven are by nature hard to make uniform; the ancients in establishing law preserved only the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: This is because things born of Heaven are by nature hard to make uniform; the ancients, in establishing law, preserved only the general outline.

sentences.zh: 故前代制尺，非特累黍，必求古雅之器以雜校焉。

translations.literal: Thus in former ages in making foot-rules, they did not rely on accumulating millet alone but necessarily sought ancient elegant vessels for mixed verification.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in former ages, when making foot-rules, they did not rely on accumulating millet alone but necessarily sought ancient elegant vessels for cross-verification.

sentences.zh: 晉泰始十年，荀勖等校定尺度，以調鐘律，是為晉之前尺。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taishi of Jin, Xun Xu and others corrected and fixed the foot-rule and measure to tune bells and pitch pipes—this is the earlier foot-rule of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Taishi of Jin, Xun Xu and others corrected and fixed the foot-rule and measure to tune bells and pitch pipes—this is the earlier Jin foot-rule.

sentences.zh: 勖等以古物七品勘之，一曰姑洗玉律，二曰小呂玉律，三曰西京銅望臬，四曰金錯望臬，五曰銅斛，六曰古錢，七曰建武銅尺。

translations.literal: Xu and others checked against seven kinds of ancient objects: first, the Maiden Washing jade pitch pipe; second, the Small Pitch jade pitch pipe; third, the Western Capital bronze wangnao; fourth, the gold-inlaid wangnao; fifth, the bronze hu; sixth, ancient coins; seventh, the Jianwu bronze foot-rule.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and others checked against seven kinds of ancient objects: first, the Maiden Washing jade pitch pipe; second, the Small Pitch jade pitch pipe; third, the Western Capital bronze wangnao; fourth, the gold-inlaid wangnao; fifth, the bronze hu; sixth, ancient coins; seventh, the Jianwu bronze foot-rule.

sentences.zh: 當時以勖尺揆校古器，與本銘尺寸無差，前史稱其用意精密。

translations.literal: At the time, using Xu's foot-rule to measure and verify against ancient vessels, there was no discrepancy with the dimensions on their inscriptions; earlier histories praise the precision of his intent.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, using Xu's foot-rule to measure and verify against ancient vessels, there was no discrepancy with the dimensions on their inscriptions; earlier histories praise the precision of his approach.

sentences.zh: 《隋志》所載諸代尺度，十有五等，然以晉之前尺為本，以其與姬周之尺、劉歆銅斛尺、建武銅尺相合。

translations.literal: The Sui Treatise records foot-rules and measures of various dynasties in fifteen grades, yet takes the earlier foot-rule of Jin as the standard, because it accords with the foot-rule of the Zhou of Ji, Liu Xin's bronze hu foot-rule, and the Jianwu bronze foot-rule.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui Treatise records foot-rules and measures of various dynasties in fifteen grades, yet takes the earlier Jin foot-rule as the standard, because it accords with the Zhou of Ji foot-rule, Liu Xin's bronze hu foot-rule, and the Jianwu bronze foot-rule.

sentences.zh: 竊惟周、漢二代，享年永久，聖賢製作，可取則焉。

translations.literal: We consider that the two dynasties of Zhou and Han enjoyed long duration, and the works of sages and worthies may be taken as models.
translations.idiomatic: We consider that the Zhou and Han dynasties endured for long ages, and the works of sages and worthies may be taken as models.

sentences.zh: 而隋氏銷毀金石，典正之物，罕復存者。

translations.literal: Yet the Sui house melted down metal and stone, and canonical correct objects rarely survive.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Sui house melted down metal and stone, and canonical standard objects rarely survive.

sentences.zh: 夫古物之有分寸，明著史籍，可以酬驗者，惟有法錢而已。

translations.literal: Among ancient objects whose fen and cun are clearly recorded in historical works and can be used for verification, there are only standard coins.
translations.idiomatic: Among ancient objects whose dimensions are clearly recorded in historical works and can be used for verification, there are only standard coins.

sentences.zh: 周之圜法，曆載曠遠，莫得而詳。

translations.literal: Zhou's round coin law extends across vast ages and cannot be known in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's round coin standard extends across vast ages and cannot be known in detail.

sentences.zh: 秦之半兩，實重八銖；

translations.literal: Qin's half-liang actually weighed eight zhu;
translations.idiomatic: The Qin dynasty 's half-liang actually weighed eight zhu;

sentences.zh: 漢初四銖，其文亦曰半兩。

translations.literal: the early Han four-zhu coin also bore the inscription half-liang.
translations.idiomatic: the early Han four-zhu coin also bore the inscription half-liang.

sentences.zh: 孝武之世始行五銖，下暨隋朝，多以五銖為號，既歷代尺度屢改，故大小輕重鮮有同者，惟劉歆置銅斛。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Xiaowu the five-zhu coin was first issued; down to the Sui dynasty, most coins bore the five-zhu designation. Since foot-rules and measures changed repeatedly through the ages, size and weight rarely matched—only Liu Xin's bronze hu.
translations.idiomatic: In the era of Emperor Wu of Han the five-zhu coin was first issued; down to the Sui dynasty, most coins bore the five-zhu designation. Since foot-rules and measures changed repeatedly through the ages, size and weight rarely matched—only Liu Xin's bronze hu.

sentences.zh: 世之所鑄錯刀並大泉五十，王莽天鳳元年改鑄貨布、貨泉之類，不聞後世復有兩者。

translations.literal: Among coins cast in the world are the cuodao and the daquan wushi; in the first year of Tianfeng of Wang Mang, huobu and huoquan and the like were recast—neither is heard of again in later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Of coins cast in the world are the cuodao and the daquan wushi; in the first year of Tianfeng of Wang Mang, huobu and huoquan and the like were recast—neither is heard of again in later ages.

sentences.zh: 臣等檢詳《漢志》、《通典》、《唐六典》云：「大泉五十，重十二銖，徑一寸二分。

translations.literal: We have examined in detail the Han Treatise, the Comprehensive Institutions, and the Six Codes of Tang, which say: "The daquan wushi weighed twelve zhu and had a diameter of one cun two fen.
translations.idiomatic: We have examined in detail the Han Treatise, the Comprehensive Institutions, and the Six Codes of Tang, which state: "The daquan wushi weighed twelve zhu and had a diameter of one cun two fen.

sentences.zh: 錯刀環如大泉，身形如刀，長二寸。

translations.literal: The cuodao had a ring like the daquan and a body like a knife, two cun long.
translations.idiomatic: The cuodao had a ring like the daquan and a body shaped like a knife, two cun long.

sentences.zh: 貨布重二十五銖，長二寸五分，廣一寸，首長八分有奇，廣八分，足股長八分，間廣二分，圍好徑二分半。

translations.literal: The huobu weighed twenty-five zhu, was two cun five fen long and one cun wide; the head was eight fen and a fraction long and eight fen wide; the foot and shank were eight fen long; the gap was two fen wide; the rim and hole had a diameter of two and a half fen.

translations.literal: The huoquan weighed five zhu and had a diameter of one cun.
translations.idiomatic: This huoquan weighed five zhu and had a diameter of one cun.

translations.literal: Some may differ slightly in size and weight from the original record, for at the time illicit casting was widespread and not all necessarily conformed to standard measure—but when the head, foot, rim, hole, length, and width all match the orthodox histories, they may be used, and then the foot-rule of the bronze hu may be known.

sentences.zh: 況經籍制度皆起周世，以劉歆術業之博，祖沖之算數之妙，荀勖揆較之詳密，校之既合周尺，則最為可法。

translations.literal: Moreover, the institutions recorded in the classics all originated in the Zhou era; given the breadth of Liu Xin's learning, the subtlety of Zu Chongzhi's computation, and the meticulousness of Xun Xu's measurements—when verified they accord with the Zhou foot-rule, and are most fit to be taken as model.

sentences.zh: 兼詳隋牛弘等議，稱後周太祖敕蘇綽造鐵尺，與宋尺同，以調中律，以均田度地。

translations.literal: Also examining in detail the discussion of Niu Hong and others of Sui, who said that Emperor Taizu of Later Zhou ordered Su Chuo to make an iron foot-rule identical to the Song foot-rule, to tune the central pitch pipe and to measure fields and land.

translations.literal: The shadow-table foot-rule of the Directorate of Astronomy today, what He Ning called the Western Capital bronze wangnao, is probably an old object from the Luoyang capital.
translations.idiomatic: This shadow-table foot-rule of the Directorate of Astronomy today, what He Ning called the Western Capital bronze wangnao, is probably an old object from the Luoyang capital.

translations.literal: The Western Capital bronze wangnao used by Xun Xu of Jin was probably an object of Western Han; He Ning called Luoyang the Western Capital, but that was Tang's eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 有唐享國三百年，其間製作法度，雖未逮周、漢，然亦可謂治安之世矣。

translations.literal: Tang held the realm for three hundred years; although the measures and institutions made in that period did not reach those of Zhou and Han, it may still be called an age of peace and good order.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang dynasty held the realm for three hundred years; although the measures and institutions made in that period did not reach those of Zhou and Han, it may still be called an age of peace and good order.

translations.literal: If the court now must seek the mean in foot-rules, it should follow the fen and cun of Han coins.
translations.idiomatic: Should the court now must seek the mean in foot-rules, it should follow the fen and cun of Han coins.

sentences.zh: 若以為太祖膺圖受禪，創制垂法，嘗詔和峴等用影表尺與典修金石，七十年間，薦之郊廟，稽合唐制，以示詒謀，則可且依影表舊尺，俟有妙達鐘律之學者，俾考正之，以從周、漢之制。

translations.literal: If one considers that the Founding Emperor received the Mandate and established institutions for posterity, and once ordered He Ning and others to use the shadow-table foot-rule in managing metal and stone ritual objects—for seventy years it was offered at suburban and temple rites, checked against Tang institutions, and shown as a legacy—then for the time being the old shadow-table foot-rule may be followed, awaiting a master versed in bells and pitch pipes to examine and correct it and return to the Zhou and Han systems.

sentences.zh: 王樸律准尺比漢錢尺寸長二分有奇，比影表尺短四分，既前代未嘗施用，復經太祖朝更易。
